portInfo.description: Port Saint John markets modern cruise terminals built in 2009 and 2012 with tidal-adjusting FMT gangways. Marco Polo (388 m) and Diamond Jubilee (340 m) are named with Yokohama fendering and large elevators/escalators; a third 301 m berth appears in the same facility list. Passenger pages highlight AREA 506 Waterfront Container Village next to Marco Polo and note peak season in the fall foliage period. Bay of Fundy tides affect the waterfront — gangway adjustability is part of the port’s published design story.

climate.description: Humid continental climate with cold winters and warm summers

politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality and itinerary. Confirm requirements with official government sources and your cruise line before travel; rules can change.
politics.entryRequirements: Valid passport usually required. Many visa-exempt visitors need an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) from the Government of Canada—confirm before you sail.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: If berthed at Marco Polo, AREA 506 is the lowest-friction first stop before climbing uptown hills.
